findings.title: Ask maintainers first writes an issue_claim outside the actions path (no action marker, no AI-assistance line)
findings.detail: proposal_actions.ask_first INSERTs the outbound_actions row directly with body CLAIM_BODY. Unlike api/actions.create_action it doesn't append '<!-- ossbot:action=<id> -->', run normalize_text, run policy.check_text with the secret values, or call control.require_running. DESIGN 12 says every comment and issue_claim body ends with that marker and that restart reconciliation (reconcile.py) finds a posted comment by it. A claim posted just before a crash is therefore not recognised, and a retry can post a second public comment. The Telegram CLAIM_BODY also drops the runner's '— drafted with AI assistance, reviewed by @{login}' line, and the button works while paused. The test checks only that a row and an approval exist. Likely also: the runner fetch stage requests a second claim after Start work, because claim_requested is never set on this path. Fix: one gatekeeper function shared by the API and the button, one claim template; test the stored bytes (marker, disclosure line) and the paused refusal.

findings.title: Rescope 'Continue at m' doesn't follow the proposal Start-work refusals and binding
findings.detail: 14.11.17 makes Continue a proposal Start work. 14.11.15 refuses Start work at Start, at Confirm and before the effect while paused, killed, draining or DOWN (workers), with the binding recomputed each time. rescope_cards.continue_first checks only the state, continue_confirm checks only approvals.system_running() (paused or killed), and continue_rescope checks nothing, so Continue goes through while draining or with the workers down. The Confirm token arg is {cid, rev}. The measured class is re-read at the second tap and rev is never compared, so a re-entered RESCOPE_REQUIRED continues on a report the panel didn't show. The transition is recorded as Actor.GATEKEEPER for a human decision. Fix: gate1_refusal at both taps and in continue_rescope; bind {rev, measured_class, sha256(size_report_json)} and refuse a mismatch; record the human actor; add draining and workers-down tests.

findings.title: Rescope 'Make it smaller' targets one class below the approved class
findings.detail: 14.11.17 (approved s, measured m) sends 'fit class s', the approved class. request_revision(kind='smaller') in RESCOPE_REQUIRED takes approved_class and steps one class down, so it asks for xs (test_rescope_card asserts 'fit class xs'). With approved xs it answers 'Already the smallest class.', leaving only Continue or Drop. Fix: in RESCOPE_REQUIRED use approved_class as the target (xs allowed); keep 'next smaller than the estimate' for the gate-1 card; update the test.

findings.title: Forbidden-paths warning on the proposal card renders scout paths without make_visible/defuse
findings.detail: proposal_cards._warnings joins scout 'areas' (free text, up to 200 chars) that match a forbidden glob, and renders them with k.line (a Const span). The text is escaped but not made visible, not defused and not labelled 🤖 (U6/U8). Because '*' matches spaces, an area like '.github/workflows/x /kill' or one with bidi controls reaches the decision card as a clickable command or disguised text. test_kit_builders never reaches this line. Fix: render the paths as k.Code(k.Text(...)) spans; add a hazard test (/kill, U+202E).

findings.title: Expired and superseded proposal cards use the PR-card copy
findings.detail: 14.11.15 asks for '⌛ Expired · re-scouting if still relevant' with [⛔ Not decidable] and the toast 'This proposal expired; a fresh one will arrive if the issue is still open.'; 14.11.16 gives superseded cards [⛔ Not decidable]. stale.render/CardPublisher.render_stale give '⌛ Expired · approval was valid 72 h' and '⛔ Not approvable', and a kit tap answers 'This proposal is no longer open.'. Branch on gate == 1.

findings.title: A 👤 v1 proposal card doesn't reply to the 'Working on it' message
findings.detail: 14.11.15 Delivery: a 👤 v1 card replies to the 'Working on it' message when that is in ✅ Reviews. CardPublisher._chain_to chains only to an earlier proposal card.

findings.title: The proposal card's Validate line labels repo facts as 🤖
findings.detail: 14.11.15 shows 'Validate ✅ repo has tests (vitest) · T0 unit · T1 n/a · 🤖 easy'. _validate_line renders 'Validate 🤖 <n> test(s) to add/update · <plan>'. Show the vet's test-runner fact and the tier with ✅.
